newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth buys footwear marketer Eastbay Inc..
newsitem.headline: Woolworth buys footwear marketer Eastbay Inc..

text.p: Woolworth Corp. said Monday it agreed to acquire Eastbay Inc., a direct marketer of athletic footwear, clothing, equipment and licensed and private label products, for about $146 million in cash.
Under the definitive agreement, Woolworth would pay $24 per share to all Eastbay shareholders except three senior Eastbay executives and principle shareholders, who would receive $22 per share.
The executives would get another $1.75 per share if certain post-closing performance targets were achieved, Woolworth said.
Eastbay's stock jumped $4.125 to $23.125 early on Nasdaq. Woolworth fell 37.5 cents to $23.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Woolworth said the deal should be completed in early 1997 and it expects Eastbay to contribute to its fiscal 1997 earnings.
Eastbay's management will remain with the company, which will operate as part of Woolworth's Athletic Group, with 3,500 stores worldwide.

"This transaction is an important step in Woolworth's strategy of aggressively growing our successful athletic footwear and apparel operations," said Roger N. Farah, chairman and chief executive of Woolworth.
"Eastbay's catalogue operations will broaden Woolworth's channels of distribution for our athletic footwear and apparel product offerings, as well as expand our customer base."
Woolworth operates almost 8,000 stores in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, including Foot Locker, Northern Reflections, Woolworth, After Thoughts and Champs Sports.
The deal has been approved by both companies' boards and remains subject to Eastbay shareholder approval, Woolworth said.
